q: What is the average review score per department for review_year 2023, counting only departments with at least 3 reviews that year? Return department name and average score.
gold: SELECT d.name, AVG(r.score) AS avg_score FROM reviews r JOIN employees e ON e.id = r.employee_id JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id WHERE r.review_year = 2023 GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3

q: For each current manager, count their current direct reports. Return the top 1 managers as (manager name, count), ordered by count descending, then manager id ascending.
gold: SELECT m.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id WHERE e.left_date IS NULL AND m.left_date IS NULL GROUP BY m.id, m.name ORDER BY n DESC, m.id LIMIT 1

q: Which former employee has the largest salary increase (current salary with the latest effective_from minus the first salary with the earliest effective_from)? Return employee id and the increase; on ties the lowest id.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT employee_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from DESC) AS rd, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from ASC) AS ra FROM salaries), c AS (SELECT employee_id, amount FROM s WHERE rd = 1), f AS (SELECT employee_id, amount FROM s WHERE ra = 1) SELECT e.id, c.amount - f.amount AS increase FROM employees e JOIN c ON c.employee_id = e.id JOIN f ON f.employee_id = e.id WHERE e.left_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY increase DESC, e.id LIMIT 1

q: Departments form a tree via parent_id with 'Corporate' at the root. For each department directly under Corporate, count the former employees in it and all its descendant departments. Return department name and headcount.
gold: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, name AS top_name FROM departments WHERE parent_id = (SELECT id FROM departments WHERE name = 'Corporate') UNION ALL SELECT d.id, t.top_name FROM departments d JOIN t ON d.parent_id = t.id) SELECT t.top_name AS name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount FROM t LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = t.id AND e.left_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.top_name

q: Among employees hired before 2021-01-01, what percentage left within 730 days of their hire date (left_date - hire_date <= 730)? Return a single number rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN left_date IS NOT NULL AND left_date - hire_date <= 730 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM employees WHERE hire_date < DATE '2021-01-01'

q: For each customer, find the date of their first 'cancelled' order. Then count customers by the calendar year of that date. Return year and count.
gold: WITH f AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS d FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM d) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS n FROM f GROUP BY yr

q: What is the average 'cancelled' order value (an order's value is the sum of quantity * order_items.unit_price over its lines) per customer country, only for countries with at least 10 such orders and excluding NULL countries? Return country and average value.
gold: WITH ov AS (SELECT o.id, c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS v FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' AND c.country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.id, c.country) SELECT country, AVG(v) AS avg_value FROM ov GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10

q: For each product category, which product earned the most revenue from 'cancelled' orders (sum of quantity * order_items.unit_price)? Return category and product name; on ties within a category pick the lowest product id.
gold: WITH r AS (SELECT p.category, p.id, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS rev FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category, p.id, p.name), k AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY rev DESC, id) AS rn FROM r) SELECT category, name FROM k WHERE rn = 1

q: How many 'pro' users made their first 'view' event in a session that was not their first session? Order sessions by started_at then session id; a user's first 'view' event is their earliest such event by ts. Return a single number.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT id, user_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY started_at, id) AS rn FROM sessions), p AS (SELECT s.user_id, s.rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY e.ts) AS prn FROM events e JOIN s ON s.id = e.session_id WHERE e.kind = 'view') SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.user_id WHERE p.prn = 1 AND p.rn > 1 AND u.plan = 'pro'

q: How many customers placed their second 'cancelled' order within 60 days (inclusive) of their first 'cancelled' order? Order by order_date, then order id, to rank orders. Return a single number.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS rn FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'), f AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date AS d1 FROM s WHERE rn = 1), g AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date AS d2 FROM s WHERE rn = 2) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM f JOIN g USING (customer_id) WHERE d2 - d1 <= 60

q: What is the average review score per department for review_year 2021, counting only departments with at least 3 reviews that year? Return department name and average score.
gold: SELECT d.name, AVG(r.score) AS avg_score FROM reviews r JOIN employees e ON e.id = r.employee_id JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id WHERE r.review_year = 2021 GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
